docs.title: Welcome
docs.text: Selena Wang, PhD selewang@iu.edu Department of Biostatistics and Health Data Science HITS 3071 410 W. 10th Street Indianapolis, IN 46202 Dr. Wang is a tenure-track Assistant Professor in the Department of Biostatistics and Health Data Science at Indiana University School of Medicine. She has an interdisciplinary background in biostatistics and computational psychology, with expertise in developing statistical and computational methods for complex, high-dimensional biomedical and networked data. Her research advances generative embedding, scalable methods and software for high-dimensional networked data, and Bayesian inference for brain and protein networks, with applications in disease subtyping, brain–behavior linkage, biomarker identification, and disease pathway discovery, particularly in Alzheimer's disease and other psychiatric and psychological conditions. Her work has been published in leading journals, including Nature Methods, Alzheimer's & Dementia, Medical Image Analysis, Psychometrika, Psychological Methods, and Human Brain Mapping. Dr. Wang has been named a William H. Gates Sr. Fellow by Alzheimer's Disease Data Initiative, a 2026 Research Career Institute in the Mental Health of Aging (CIMA) Scholar and a 2025 Research Education Component (REC) Scholar of the Indiana Alzheimer's Disease Research Center. Her methodological research program is supported by the Alzheimer's Disease Data Initiative and the National Institute on Aging.

docs.title: Postdoctoral Fellow
docs.text: Dr. Jaeyoung Lee                      Dr. Jaeyoung Lee is a postdoctoral fellow in the lab. He received his doctoral training in Statistics at Virginia Tech, where his dissertation focused on supervised variational autoencoder frameworks for predictive modeling and association analysis. His research interests include heterogeneous data learning, deep generative models, variational inference, Bayesian methods, latent space models, dimension reduction, and statistical machine learning. In the lab, he develops statistical and machine learning methods for high-dimensional biomedical and neuroimaging data.

docs.title: Ph.D. Students
docs.text: Renhao Li                      Renhao Li is a Ph.D. student working with our team. His research focuses on statistical and computational methods for high-dimensional biomedical data, with interests in network modeling, machine learning, and neuroimaging applications.                  Luling Altan                      Luling Altan is a Ph.D. student in SWLab. Her research focuses on developing Bayesian methodology for complex networks, particularly brain and protein networks. She suspects that much of what we observe is a projection from a much higher-dimensional space, and that the most interesting part of a dataset often lies in its latent structure rather than the features we directly measure. With a background in mathematics, she is drawn to graph theory and its applications in neuroscience for this reason.                                       In her spare time, she loves rock climbing, researching the art of raising cats, reading about Vedic astrology, photographing nebulae and galaxies, and predicting people's destinies with star charts.

docs.title: Research
docs.text: Network science is interdisciplinary. Focusing on improving current analytical strategies, we try to absorb influences of other disciplines to inform and improve understandings about human behaviors with applications in neuroscience, psychiatry, psychology and others. Broadly speaking, we model real-world networks with statistically sound principles and methods—reduce network complexity, perform intuitive visualization and test critical hypotheses with improved statistical power and controlled type I errors. We are particularly interested in the topological structures of networks and the roles they play in (neuro)degeneration, (neuro)development and resilience.

docs.title: Topics we are currently working on
Network-based neuroimaging methodology development
docs.text: Statistical network methods for brain–behavior linking, connectome-based inference, trajectory and normative modeling, interplay between functional and structural connectivity, brain-age research, imaging harmonization, and imaging genetics.

docs.title: Alzheimer's disease, neurodegeneration, and resilience
docs.text: Modeling the co-evolution of brain connectomes and pathological proteins, understanding individual differences in Alzheimer's disease progression, and identifying network mechanisms underlying cognitive resilience.

docs.title: Multimodal neuroimaging and molecular data integration
docs.text: Integrating neuroimaging with genetics, transcriptomics, proteomics, molecular and cellular information, and other biological biomarkers to understand the biological mechanisms underlying brain organization, aging, and neurodegeneration.

docs.title: Statistical machine learning and AI
docs.text: Generative and representation-learning methods for high-dimensional biomedical data, including deep learning, embedding, clustering, prediction versus inference, and interpretable statistical machine learning.

docs.title: Higher-order and complex network modeling
docs.text: Statistical methods for complex network structures, including hypergraphs, latent space models, network diffusion, and higher-order interactions among brain regions, biological systems, and behavioral outcomes.

docs.title: JNIRM
docs.text: An R package for estimating the Joint Network and Item Response Model (JNIRM), integrating social network structures with item response data.

docs.title: jlsm
docs.text: An R package for estimating joint latent space models for social networks and multivariate attributes using a fast inference approach.

docs.title: Prospective Students
docs.text:
(2026) I am looking for motivated students to contribute to complex networks and systems research to investigate biomedical complexity at the SWLab. The SWLab is housed within the department of biostatistics and health data science at IU School of Medicine. The lab focuses on applying and developing scalable statistical and computational approaches for high-dimensional biomedical data with emphases on network science, high dimensional data analysis, neuroimaging, data integration and statistical machine learning. Depending on prior experiences, selected candidates will have the opportunity to contribute to substantive neuroscience research, method innovations or software development and documentation.

If you possess the following qualifications, I strongly encourage you to consider applying:

  1. Have a background or prior experience in neuroimaging, network analysis, or computational neuroscience.
  2. Skilled in programming and/or statistical method development.

If you are interested in joining my lab, please email me the following documents with the subject “Prospective student for SWLab”:

  1. Your CV
  2. A brief description of your background and interest
